L2t: Hospitals often ask patients to bring personal toiletries, including shavers, from home.
L3t: Shared or reused razors can carry blood and skin particles, so a personal razor avoids passing infection between patients.
L4t: Male patients are told to bring their own electric razor to minimise the risk of cross-infection from shared equipment.
L2f: Hospital wards usually have fixed daily routines for washing, meals, and visiting hours.
L3f: Patients who bring their own razor can shave whenever they like rather than waiting for ward staff or shared equipment, which is the point of the advice.
L4f: Male patients are advised to bring their own electric razor so they can shave at a time that suits them.
